subject: gk
question: Which of the following is a typical example of Revenue Expenditure?

options.text: Purchase of land for a PSU facility
Interest paid on a government loan

solution:
The correct answer is __**Interest paid on a government loan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Revenue expenditure** refers to the expenses incurred by the government for its day-to-day functioning and maintenance of services.
 
• Interest paid on a government loan is considered revenue expenditure as it does not result in the creation of assets or reduction of liabilities.
 
• It is a recurring expense that is necessary to meet the financial obligations of the government.
 
• Such expenditures are reported in the revenue account of the government budget and are essential for maintaining fiscal stability.
 
• Examples of other revenue expenditures include salaries, pensions, subsidies, and administrative costs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Construction of a railway terminal (Option 1)**
 
 
• This involves the creation of new infrastructure, which is classified as **capital expenditure**.
 
• Capital expenditure results in the creation of assets and is aimed at long-term benefits.
 
 
 
• **Purchase of land for a PSU facility (Option 2)**
 
 
• The acquisition of land is also categorized as **capital expenditure**.
 
• It is considered an investment that contributes to the development of public assets.
 
 
 
• **Funding a national highway project (Option 4)**
 
 
• Expenditure on infrastructure projects like highways is a part of **capital expenditure**.
 
• Such spending is focused on asset creation and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Expenditure Overview**
 
 
• Revenue expenditure does not lead to asset creation or liability reduction.
 
• It is incurred to maintain the existing assets and services.
 
• Examples include interest payments, grants to states, and subsidies.
 
• It is essential for the smooth functioning of government operations in the short term.
